_why: ADR 0024 moved the assembler into the enclave, so the strings an agent
reads are now produced in Rust. The Python assembler produced them until
now and still does on the paths A1 has not reached, and clients parse
them. Two implementations of one format drift, and the drift is silent:
nothing errors, the citations just stop lining up with the lines.
This file is the format. Each side builds a node from the descriptor,
formats it, and compares against `expected`. Neither side owns it, which
is the point -- a change here has to be made deliberately and fails both

lines.case: an active claim carries no status marker, because active is the ordinary case
a superseded claim is shown rather than hidden, and says so
a contradicted claim too: an unresolved disagreement is still evidence
an event is its summary; the body never reaches a line
an entity leads with its kind, which is the one line that does
and the kind is the serde spelling, not the Python enum name

declines.case: nothing retrieved at all is not a permission problem and must not read like one
everything retrieved was out of scope: the count and the reasons, nothing else
declines.expected: Declining to answer: 1 candidate memory object(s) matched, but none are within the requesting agent's scope (too sensitive).

declines.case: reasons are deduplicated and sorted, so the same denial set reads the same way twice
declines.expected: Declining to answer: 3 candidate memory object(s) matched, but none are within the requesting agent's scope (too sensitive, wrong owner).
